q: How many watts of lighting per square metre should a factory shop floor use?
title: Lighting watts per square metre in a factory
short: BEE's MSME guidelines, drawing on the Energy Conservation Building Code, give lighting power density ranges of 6.0 to 12.0 W per square metre for process shop floors lit to 150 to 300 lux, 7.1 to 14.1 for workshops, 3.5 to 7.08 for warehouses and 5.0 to 9.5 for office buildings.
audience: Factory owners, electrical contractors and energy auditors sizing a lighting retrofit

ul: Administrative building, 50 to 400 lux: 5.0 to 9.5 W per square metre
Shop floor process lighting, 150 to 300 lux: 6.0 to 12.0
Warehouse storage area, 100 to 150 lux: 3.5 to 7.08

p: Add up the rated watts of every fitting in the area, including drivers or ballasts, and divide by the floor area in square metres. Then check the light level with a lux meter: a low figure with dark corners is not a win.

sections.h: If you are above the range
ul: Replace old tube lights, mercury vapour and metal halide fittings with LEDs.
Re-space fittings to the task instead of lighting every square metre evenly.
Add daylight and controls; BEE also suggests solar tubes and solar PV lighting where feasible.

example.title: Example: a 1,000 square metre shop floor (illustrative)
lines: Before: 100 fittings of 150 W = 15,000 W; 15,000 / 1,000 = 15 W per square metre, above the 6.0 to 12.0 range
After: 100 LED high-bays of 90 W = 9,000 W; 9 W per square metre, inside the range
At 3,000 hours a year the change saves 6 kW x 3,000 = 18,000 kWh
example.note: Wattages and hours are illustrative. Confirm the light level on the floor after the change.
